newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa JSE turnover up 85.6 pct year-on-year.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa JSE turnover up 85.6 pct year-on-year.

text.p: Turnover on South Africa's Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), excluding arbitrage deals, surged 85.6 percent in the 12 months to December 31, 1996, compared to the same period in 1995, JSE statistics show.
Trade worth 117.36 billion rand was concluded between January and December, 1996, up from 63.25 billion rand in the same period in 1995.
Net foreign purchases on the bourse stood at 5.25 billion rand in 1996, up from 4.81 billion purchased in 1995, the JSE said.
Liquidity until the end of December, 1996, had improved to 10.9 percent from 7.1 percent the previous year.
The market capitalisation of the bourse rose to 1,130 billion rand in the calender year to December 31, 1996, up from 1,023 billion in the calender year ended December, 1995.
The JSE said its overall 100 percent index rose 6.9 percent to 6,658 in 1996 while the all gold 100 percent index was 12.1 percent stronger. The industrial 100 percent index was down 0.8 percent.
